title: Thread-Safe Singleton
question: Implement a thread-safe Singleton pattern. Requirements: 1) Lazy initialization, 2) Thread-safe, 3) No performance overhead after initialization, 4) Prevent reflection attacks. Discuss: using double-checked locking with volatile, enum singleton approach (best practice), lazy holder idiom, synchronized method approach, comparing tradeoffs, explaining why volatile is needed in DCL, handling serialization with readResolve(), and preventing reflection with enum or exception throwing.

title: Producer-Consumer Implementation
question: Implement producer-consumer pattern with multiple producers and consumers. Requirements: 1) Use BlockingQueue, 2) Handle graceful shutdown, 3) Process 1M messages, 4) No message loss, 5) Bounded queue. Discuss: using LinkedBlockingQueue with capacity, implementing producer threads that add messages, implementing consumer threads that process messages, handling InterruptedException, using poison pill pattern for shutdown, implementing ExecutorService for thread management, monitoring queue size, handling backpressure, and ensuring all messages are processed before shutdown.

title: Custom Thread Pool
question: Design and implement a custom thread pool. Requirements: 1) Fixed number of worker threads, 2) Task queue, 3) Graceful shutdown, 4) Rejected execution policy, 5) Thread naming. Discuss: maintaining a queue of Runnable tasks, creating fixed number of worker threads, implementing run loop that takes tasks from queue, using BlockingQueue for thread-safe task queue, implementing submit() method to add tasks, implementing shutdown() and shutdownNow(), handling rejected tasks when queue is full, naming threads for debugging, implementing monitoring (active threads, completed tasks), and comparing with ThreadPoolExecutor.

title: Immutable Class with Mutable Fields
question: Create an immutable class that contains mutable objects. Requirements: 1) Class has Date and List fields, 2) Truly immutable, 3) No defensive copying overhead in getters. Discuss: making class final, making all fields private final, deep copying mutable objects in constructor, returning copies or unmodifiable views from getters, using Collections.unmodifiableList(), creating defensive Date copies, considering performance vs safety tradeoffs, and using immutable collections (Guava, Java 9+).

title: Custom Validation Annotation
question: Create a custom annotation @Email that validates email addresses. Requirements: 1) Works on fields, 2) Compile-time retention for reflection, 3) Validation logic, 4) Integration with bean validation. Discuss: creating @Email annotation with @Target(FIELD), using @Retention(RUNTIME), defining message attribute, creating EmailValidator class implementing ConstraintValidator, implementing validation logic with regex, registering validator, using reflection to process annotations, integrating with JSR 303/380, and handling validation errors.

title: Deadlock Detection and Resolution
question: Implement a system to detect and resolve deadlocks. Requirements: 1) Monitor thread states, 2) Detect circular wait, 3) Log deadlock information, 4) Prevent deadlocks with lock ordering. Discuss: using ThreadMXBean to detect deadlocks, implementing periodic deadlock detection, identifying threads involved in deadlock, logging stack traces, implementing lock ordering strategy (always acquire locks in same order), using tryLock() with timeout, implementing deadlock prevention with resource hierarchy, creating monitoring dashboard, and designing recovery mechanism.

title: Custom Stream Collector
question: Implement a custom Collector that groups elements and maintains order. Requirements: 1) Group by key, 2) Maintain insertion order, 3) Support parallel streams, 4) Efficient. Discuss: implementing Collector interface with Supplier, Accumulator, Combiner, and Finisher, using LinkedHashMap for order, handling parallel execution with proper combining, implementing characteristics (CONCURRENT, UNORDERED), comparing with Collectors.groupingBy(), optimizing for performance, and handling edge cases (null keys, empty streams).

title: Memory Leak Investigation
question: Debug a memory leak in production application. Requirements: 1) Application runs out of memory after 2 days, 2) Heap dumps show increasing HashMap size, 3) Map is used as cache, 4) No explicit cleanup. Discuss: taking heap dump with jmap, analyzing with MAT/VisualVM, identifying growing collections, checking for static references, reviewing cache implementation, implementing WeakHashMap for cache, using SoftReference for memory-sensitive cache, implementing cache eviction policy (LRU), setting max size limits, monitoring memory usage, implementing cleanup thread, and considering external cache (Redis, Caffeine).
